_readme: Manually researched signals for the NorthStar Anesthesia ABM Signal Tracker, gathered via real web research (batch-by-batch, 5 companies at a time) while the permanent Sheets-based signal pipeline is being wired up. Each entry becomes one row in the 'alerts_sent' table via seed_northstar_signals.py. signal_type must be one of the canonical strings tracker/signal_score.py and tracker/dashboard_builder.py expect: 'Funding Round', 'Acquisition / M&A', 'IPO Signal', 'C-Suite Join', 'C-Suite Exit', 'News Mention', 'Product Launch', 'Partnership', 'Creative Hiring' (this last one is displayed to NorthStar as 'Anesthesiologists' via the hiring_opts override in build_northstar_dashboard.py -- the stored key stays 'Creative Hiring' so the shared scoring engine needs only one constant). confidence (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW, from the research pass) is written straight into the 'severity' column -- it is the closest available proxy for alert importance and is what actually drives the dashboard's H/M/L counts.

_quality_bar.why: This feed drives real sales outreach for an anesthesia staffing and perioperative management company. A signal earns its place only if it changes who a rep calls, when they call, or what they open with. Volume is not the goal; a short feed of real buying windows beats a long one padded with press releases.
include_HIGH: The account is recruiting anesthesiologists or CRNAs itself (self-staffing, so displaceable or supplementable). Name the facility, comp, and whether it is one req or a team.
The incumbent anesthesia group or staffing vendor is identified (who NorthStar would displace).
New or added operating rooms, new surgical hospitals, new ASCs, OR or perioperative capacity expansion.
Surgical volume or acuity going up: robotic fleet purchases, OR throughput programs, a shift to higher-acuity service lines.
Ownership change at the account: M&A, merger, JV, PE or health-system takeover. Contracts get reviewed when owners change.
A new CEO, COO, CFO, CMO, or perioperative/surgical-services leader, or an open vacancy in one of those roles.
An existing NorthStar relationship or contract at the account (account-team context, and label it as such).
include_MEDIUM: Non-OR facility growth attached to a surgical hospital (beds, towers, attached ERs).
Financial growth or fresh capital that funds surgical expansion.
Division-level or MSO-level leadership change one step removed from the contract owner.
A single robot deployment or a single ASC joining a platform.
Instability worth a call: service-line closure, physician group attrition, ownership litigation.
exclude_always: Awards, rankings, 'best of' or 'most awarded' lists, Healthgrades/US News/Newsweek/Leapfrog honours, anniversaries, individual physician honours. Recognition is not intent.
Rollup or summary signals that restate specific signals already logged, and the same job req cross-posted to a second board.
Events superseded by a later logged event (log the current state, not the whole history).

Firmographics dressed as events: 'their site says they use X', 'person confirmed in role as of'. If there is no dated event, it is not a signal, and a today-stamped non-event never ages out of the 90-day windows.

Anything with no path to anesthesia demand: payer or health-plan network contracting, medspa and aesthetics, unrelated compliance settlements, venture investments in unrelated tech, academic faculty posts, PR and research milestones.
NorthStar's own job reqs logged as the prospect's hiring intent. That inverts the read: it means NorthStar already holds the contract, so log it as Partnership.
rules: Prefer specifics over aggregates. Facility name, OR count, comp figure, and date are what make a signal usable.
Every claim needs a real fetchable source URL. An empty category is a good and expected result; reporting nothing beats guessing.
signal_date must be the date the event happened, not the date it was researched. Use a today-stamp only for a genuinely live job posting.
Severity is importance to an anesthesia pitch, not confidence in the source. If most rows are HIGH, the tile has stopped filtering anything.

Exec-change signals carry a finite buying window of roughly 12 to 18 months. Past that, drop them to MEDIUM: knowing who holds the seat is context, not a trigger. Capacity facts (operating rooms, facilities, ownership) do not decay the same way and keep their severity.
Facility growth is HIGH only when it adds operating rooms or surgical capacity. Outpatient clinics, freestanding ERs, rehab towers, and medical office buildings are footprint, not anesthesia demand.
Calibrate severity to scale. A 49-robot fleet purchase and one da Vinci at one ASC are not the same signal; a 35-facility M&A year and one ASC joining a platform are not either.
A CEO transition is legitimately two rows (C-Suite Exit for the outgoing person, C-Suite Join for the incoming one): they are two different contacts. That is not a duplicate.
Prune as well as add. Re-run the seed with --prune so the JSON stays the single source of truth.
